answer: Each agent must put stake on-chain before its messages count, and a randomly selected committee slashes that stake if it signs conflicting actions under the same identity. This does not prove a real person is behind an agent; it makes a Sybil swarm costly because every additional identity needs separately locked capital and risks losing it. An attacker can still buy influence, but must expose funds to forfeiture rather than minting identities for free. Think of onyx, velvet, and crystal as three names competing for seats: each must post its own bond.
